lessons.title: Avere or essere in the past
lessons.objective: Avere or essere in the past: Most verbs form the passato prossimo with avere, and the participle keeps -o: ho pagato.
lessons.explanation:

Sono arrivata prima dei miei colleghi. — I arrived before my coworkers.

lessons.title: Stato, avuto and potuto in the past
lessons.objective: Stato, avuto and potuto in the past: Essere takes essere in the past, with the participle stato (è stato, è stata), and avere takes avere (ho avuto).

Ho avuto un appuntamento in centro. — I had an appointment downtown.

lessons.title: The passato remoto in stories
lessons.objective: The passato remoto in stories: Written stories often use the passato remoto, mostly in the third person: dormì, dormirono; ripeté, ripeterono.
lessons.explanation:
Written stories often use the passato remoto, mostly in the third person: dormì, dormirono; ripeté, ripeterono. Some common verbs are irregular: chiedere → chiese, chiesero; fare → fece; venire → venne. In everyday speech the same events take the passato prossimo (ha chiesto).
Mio cugino chiese una camera tranquilla. — My cousin asked for a quiet room.
La receptionist ripeté il numero del piano. — The receptionist repeated the floor number.

lessons.objective: Imperfetto for background: The imperfetto describes background, ongoing conditions and past habits: -avo for -are, -evo for -ere, -ivo for -ire.

lessons.title: Two object pronouns
lessons.objective: Two object pronouns: When two object pronouns go together, the indirect one comes first and mi, ti, ci, vi become me, te, ce, ve: me lo, te la.

lessons.objective: Reflexive and reciprocal meanings: Reflexive pronouns (mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si) show an action directed at oneself; with a plural subject, ci, vi and si can also mean each other.

lessons.title: Plan around an uncertain forecast
lessons.objective: Plan around an uncertain forecast: The futuro semplice adds -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno to the infinitive stem, with -are changing to -er- and irregular stems such as andr-, avr-, dovr-, sar- and far-.
lessons.explanation:
The futuro semplice adds -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno to the infinitive stem, with -are changing to -er- and irregular stems such as andr-, avr-, dovr-, sar- and far-. Verbs in -care and -gare add h to keep the hard sound (cercheremo, pagherò), and a plan that is already fixed often takes the present: partiamo presto.

Partiamo presto perché abbiamo già i biglietti. — We are leaving early because we already have the tickets.
